actions.action: Check whether the metal planter has a drainage hole
Move the plant into a pot with drainage
Alternatively, set the nursery pot inside the metal planter so water can drain
Remove the plant and inspect the roots
Trim brown, mushy roots if present
Repot in fresh chunky aroid mix with perlite or bark
Check that the top 2-3 inches of soil are dry before watering
Water thoroughly and empty the saucer
Move the plant to bright, indirect light
Trim fully brown leaf parts with clean scissors
Wash tools between cuts if bacterial
Monitor the spotted leaves for spreading
Isolate the plant if the spots spread
Post a photo of the roots when repotting

reason: The answer identifies the wet soil and undrained pot as the main issue and notes that low light is causing stretched growth; its core advice (drainage pot, chunky aroid mix, brighter light) matches the fix, and nothing in it is harmful.
